note: expected lists only YES/UNCLEAR entries; any gate not listed is expected NO for that case

cases.customerText: My latest invoice charged me twice for the same month. Please correct it and refund the extra charge.
The broadband has been completely dead since this morning. The router shows a red light and nothing I do helps.
I want to upgrade my mobile subscription to the 20 GB plan. How do I do that?
Your agent was rude to me on the phone yesterday and hung up while I was still explaining the problem.
cases.rationale: Clear interaction complaint with negative affect.

cases.customerText: Cancel my subscription effective immediately.
cases.rationale: Direct cancellation instruction; also contract lifecycle and by definition churn.

cases.customerText: I was promised a refund of the setup fee three weeks ago and the money still has not arrived.
cases.rationale: Refund not delivered; promised earlier = unresolved.

cases.customerText: The WiFi keeps dropping every evening around nine. It has happened every day this week.
Thank you so much! The technician came today and everything works perfectly now. Excellent service.
Why has my monthly price gone up by 40 kronor without any warning? I never agreed to a price change.
I want to close my broadband subscription and my TV package at the end of next month.
Your support line kept me waiting 47 minutes and then cut me off. This is the second time this week.
The TV streaming app crashes every time I try to watch live sports. Reinstalling did not help.
Can you send me a copy of my current contract? I want to check the notice period.
I have been charged for a premium channel I never ordered. Remove it and refund the last two months.
This is completely unacceptable. The internet has been unstable for two weeks and nothing happens no matter how many times I report it.
I am moving to a new apartment on the first of the month and need my broadband moved with me.
Your staff member Maria was fantastic, patient and solved my email problem in ten minutes. Give her a raise!
My payment failed twice this month even though my card is fine. Now I have received a late fee on top.
I do not want to continue after this month. Please terminate the mobile subscription then.
The new router you sent is faulty - it restarts itself randomly several times a day.
Support was very friendly, but the connection is still broken and I have already started looking at Telia's offers.
I was overcharged again this month, the third incorrect invoice in a row, and your chat support just ended the conversation without helping.
The broadband keeps cutting out, I have called three times about it, and honestly I am starting to wonder why I stay with Nordbo at all.
I want to downgrade my TV package and also complain that the streaming quality has been terrible lately.
Refund still not received after a month, my emails are ignored, and Tele2 has a better deal for half your price.
Moving house on Friday, need the service moved, and while we are at it: last invoice had a charge for a film I never ordered.
Every winter the same connectivity problems return. Your technician fixed it in autumn but by December it was back. I am tired of reporting this.
Thanks for sorting the invoice mistake so quickly! However the router you sent as replacement is dead on arrival.
cases.rationale: Mixed positive + new fault + billing context.

cases.customerText: I want to add my daughter to my subscription and complain about the rude man in your store who refused to help me yesterday.
The price increase notice arrived the same week the internet broke for two days. I have started comparing other providers' prices this weekend.
Second month in a row with a wrong bill, and every time I call I get a different explanation. Nobody calls back as promised.
Please cancel the sports package I added last month, it costs too much and I barely watch it anyway.
cases.rationale: Package removal = contract change with cost motive; not full cancellation.

cases.customerText: Your app is buggy and the support chat is a robot loop that never reaches a human. I regret choosing Nordbo.
cases.rationale: App fault + interaction frustration; regret is affect, not churn intent.

cases.customerText: Broadband installed yesterday, technician was great, but I was billed the installation fee I was told would be waived.
The connection failed during my work video calls twice today. If I lose one more client because of this I will have to look for another provider.
I asked for a new SIM three weeks ago, nothing has arrived, and the tracking case was closed without anyone telling me.
cases.rationale: Order not delivered + case closed silently.

cases.customerText: Mobile data has been slow in my area for months, complaints go nowhere, and Telenor advertises double speed for less money.
cases.rationale: Slow data + competitor comparison with intent.

cases.customerText: Great that the outage compensation was approved. The claim form was however impossible to use on mobile.
I need to end the contract for my late father's line and transfer his number to my own subscription. Also please stop the invoices for his account.
cases.rationale: Cancellation of one line + transfer + billing stop.

cases.customerText: Support solved my email issue quickly, but the same problem returned this morning, and the agent promised it would not.
Something is not right with my account lately.
cases.rationale: Too vague to place a topic.

cases.customerText: It happened again.
I am not sure I made the right choice switching to you people.
The thing you sent does not seem to do what it is supposed to.
Is this really how it is supposed to work?
There seems to be some mistake somewhere on your side.
I have been thinking about our arrangement.
Not entirely happy with how things have gone, to be honest.
The number on the paper and the number in the app do not match.
Someone should look into what happened in March.
A friend recommended I check what else is out there.
Your service and my patience are both getting worse.
cases.rationale: Affect expressed; deterioration implies recurring trouble.

cases.customerText: It was better before the change.
Do I really need to explain this again?
The box makes a strange noise sometimes.
If the broadband fails one more time, I am switching provider.
cases.rationale: Design example: conditional churn, not cancellation.

cases.customerText: Telia seems better than this.
cases.rationale: Competitor praise; switching intent not expressed.

cases.customerText: When does my contract end? I would like to know my options.
cases.rationale: Contract-end question; leaving overtones but no instruction.

cases.customerText: This service is terrible.
cases.rationale: Design example: dissatisfaction alone is not churn.

cases.customerText: How much notice do I need to give if I ever decide to end the contract?
cases.rationale: Hypothetical ending question; not an instruction.

cases.customerText: I am thinking about switching.
cases.rationale: Design example: consideration is churn risk, not cancellation.

cases.customerText: If this happens again, I will cancel.
cases.rationale: Design example: conditional future intent is churn, not cancellation.

cases.customerText: What is the procedure for cancelling, just so I know?
cases.rationale: Process question; actual instruction not clearly given.

cases.customerText: The internet is slow but only when it rains. Should a modern network behave like that?
Your competitor sent me a letter with a 199 kronor offer. Interesting.
cases.rationale: Competitor offer noted; interest level unclear.

cases.customerText: I asked how to keep my number if I ever move to another operator. Just curious.
cases.rationale: Portability question with 'just curious' - borderline churn.

cases.customerText: Fix the connection or we will see about the future of this subscription.
cases.rationale: Veiled conditional threat to the relationship.

cases.customerText: The invoice is correct this month, I just find the layout confusing.
cases.rationale: Invoice mention without a billing problem.

cases.customerText: Your prices are not exactly cheap, are they?
I would like to pause my subscription for the summer months.
cases.rationale: Pause is a contract change, not cancellation.

cases.customerText: Yesterday I was ready to cancel everything, but support fixed the problem and I have decided to stay.
cases.rationale: Design example: current state matters; past churn resolved.

cases.customerText: I complained about slow speeds for months. After the router swap last week it is finally fast again. Consider me satisfied.
I was going to leave you for Telia, but their install fee changed my mind. For now I am staying.
cases.rationale: Competitor considered and rejected; churn currently no.

cases.customerText: The outage on Tuesday was awful, but the compensation credit you applied is fair. Water under the bridge.
I already sent a cancellation request last month but nobody processed it. I am still here and still being billed. Please confirm what is happening!
cases.rationale: Standing cancellation request unprocessed; current state = still customer.

cases.customerText: First your support was rude, then a different agent called back and could not have been nicer. Mixed feelings.
We were about to switch the whole family to another operator, but your retention team offered a deal we accepted. All good now.
The line was dead all morning, then it came back by itself around noon. No idea what you did, but thanks I guess.
cases.rationale: Fault occurred; currently resolved; lukewarm thanks not real praise.

cases.customerText: I said I would quit if the price went up. It went up. I have not decided what to do yet.
cases.rationale: Condition met but decision pending = live churn risk, not cancellation.

cases.customerText: After my complaint your technician visited twice: the first visit fixed nothing, the second seems to have solved it. Fingers crossed.
cases.rationale: Fault history with cautious current resolution.

cases.customerText: Hello, I have been a customer for eleven years, first with mobile, then broadband, then TV. In all that time I have maybe complained twice. But now: on the 3rd I noticed the invoice was 549 instead of 399. I downloaded the PDF, checked every line, and found a 'service activation fee' nobody mentioned. I called on the 5th, waited 30 minutes, was told it was a mistake and would be refunded in five working days. On the 12th still no refund. I emailed, got an autoreply, then nothing. Meanwhile my neighbour says her provider includes the sports channels for less. I am not the kind of person who threatens anything, but my patience has limits. Kindly fix the invoice and confirm the refund.
cases.rationale: Noisy long letter: refund + ignoring + neighbour comparison + 'patience has limits'.

cases.customerText: Dear Nordbo, I write regarding ticket 88123 opened on the 14th and ticket 90455 opened on the 22nd, both about packet loss on the evening network in my area. I have attached ping logs, traceroutes, and screenshots. I rebooted the router as advised, tried the spare router as advised, and moved the router away from the microwave as advised. The problem persists between 20:00 and 23:00 daily. I work evenings and this affects my livelihood. Your technicians are polite and clearly try, but the advice cycle repeats itself. I request escalation to someone who can examine the area infrastructure rather than my kitchen appliances.
cases.rationale: Deep technical detail, repeat contacts, polite staff (no interaction complaint), no churn signal.

cases.customerText: Long story short: broadband installed in spring, never quite stable, four engineer visits, three routers, two compensation credits (appreciated), one angry tweet (deleted). My partner thinks we should just move to cable. I keep telling her the mobile bundle discount makes it complicated. Anyway, the point of this message: the connection dropped during my daughter's school video exam this morning and the school is asking questions. Please treat this with some urgency.
cases.rationale: Noisy family story; cable consideration by partner; urgency request.

cases.customerText: I am writing on behalf of my mother, who is 81 and your customer since the nineties. She recently moved to assisted living. We need to: 1) cancel her broadband at the old address, 2) keep her mobile number, 3) understand the final invoice which includes something called a 'cessation fee', and 4) complain that when she called herself, the agent apparently told her 'these things are complicated for older people'. She was upset for days. I trust we can sort this out properly.
cases.rationale: Third-party cancellation + fees + discriminatory treatment remark.

cases.customerText: Hi! Not a complaint, more of a question plus some feedback. I saw your campaign about the new TV box and wondered if existing customers can get it, and whether it fixes the HDR glitch my current box has had since the spring update (I mentioned it once, nothing came of it, but it is minor). Also, whoever redesigned the bill layout deserves praise, I can finally understand it. That is all. Have a nice weekend!
cases.rationale: Upgrade question + old minor fault + praise; friendly tone.

cases.customerText: To whom it may concern. Reference: account 4471. Re: repeated overcharging. Chronology: January invoice +60 (roaming, disputed, credited in February after two calls). March invoice +60 again (same roaming flag). April: credited after one call, agent admitted a system bug. May: +60 again. I have now been credited three times for the same non-existent roaming and billed for it four times. I no longer wish to spend my lunch breaks on this. If the May invoice is not corrected permanently I will consider my options, including the ombudsman and other providers.

Good afternoon. First, praise: Anna in retention was wonderful when my contract renewal came up, clear about prices, no pressure. Because of her I renewed for two years even though I had a Telenor quote on my desk. Second, a concern: since the renewal the app shows my old plan, the new discount is missing, and the projected next invoice is wrong by about 90. Third, a small thing: the confirmation email addressed me as 'Mr Null'.
cases.rationale: Renewal + competitor quote rejected + pricing display errors.

cases.customerText: I run a small cafe and use your business broadband. Since the street works in June the connection degrades whenever it rains - I have correlated this over six weeks with my card terminal failures (card payments fail, customers walk out, I lose real money). I reported it twice; both times your line tests 'show no fault' because it was dry those days. I am attaching weather data. I do not want compensation, I want it fixed. If it helps, the cafe two doors down on another network has no issues when it rains.
cases.rationale: Correlated fault narrative; other-network mention is evidence more than switching intent, so churn UNCLEAR-less; marked competitor mention only.

cases.customerText: So here is the story: I ordered the family bundle in November. Installation appointment one: technician never showed (I took a day off). Appointment two: wrong router. Appointment three: works, but the TV part was never activated. Four phone calls, one chat, one email. Meanwhile the invoices started arriving for the full bundle including the TV I cannot watch. Each person I spoke to was individually nice, and I do not blame them, but as a system you are failing me. My wife asks daily why we switched to you. Please: activate the TV, fix the invoices, and someone own this case end to end.
cases.rationale: Order saga; staff individually nice so interaction complaint UNCLEAR-leaning-no, system failure expressed; spousal regret = churn overtones.

cases.customerText: Dear customer service, I will try to be brief because I know you are busy. Since the spring, the email address included with my subscription intermittently rejects my password. I have reset it perhaps twenty times. Your help articles are of no use. The chatbot insists my problem is about invoices, which it is not. Yesterday I finally reached a human who fixed something on the server side, and it worked - for four hours. This morning, locked out again. I write novels for a living and my correspondence is with publishers; this is not a trivial hobby account. I would like this treated as the serious ongoing fault it is.
cases.rationale: Email fault saga; chatbot misrouting frustration.

cases.customerText: I am not cancelling. I just want you to fix the connection.
I have no intention of leaving, but the invoice really must be corrected.
Do NOT close my account. I am only updating my payment card details.
Everyone told me I would regret switching to you, but honestly I have never been happier with a provider.
The problem is not the internet, it is your app that cannot show my data usage correctly.
cases.rationale: Negates one fault, asserts another (still technical).

cases.customerText: I would never cancel by email anyway. Speaking of which, when is the paper invoice being sent?
cases.rationale: Cancellation words in procedural discussion only; invoice logistics question.

cases.customerText: No, the router is not broken. The problem is definitely on your end of the line.
cases.rationale: Negates equipment fault, asserts line fault.

cases.customerText: I am not angry, I am disappointed. There is a difference. The outages continue.
cases.rationale: Denies anger while expressing disappointment - still negative affect.

cases.customerText: Thanks in advance for fixing the billing error. Unlike your competitor, you usually sort things out.
cases.rationale: Politeness formula + real praise; competitor mention is contrastive.

cases.customerText: I do not want to cancel anything. I want to ADD the movie package. Also, the price of that package is outrageous, but fine.
cases.rationale: Cancellation negated; add-on request; price gripe without dispute.
